sections.label: 1 - EVERY EVENT THAT COUNTS
sections.note: One webhook, fed by a GHL workflow per event type. New lead, appointment booked or updated, call outcome, contract sent, payment received. Every one arrives in the same shape.

sections.label: 2 - CREDIT THE RIGHT REP
sections.note: This is the part that gets scorecards wrong. A booked call is credited to the assigned user on the calendar event, not to whoever owns the contact. Nothing gets counted until a rep is resolved.

sections.label: 3 - WRITE THE RAW ROW
sections.note: Every event lands on an Events tab, one row, timestamped. The scorecard is always rebuildable from it, so a bad number can be traced to the event that caused it.

sections.label: 4 - THE SCORECARD
sections.note: Once a night the events roll up per rep into leads, booked, held, contracts, revenue, and the ratios that actually get coached on. One row per rep per day, plus a leaderboard in Slack.

sections.label: 5 - NOTHING FAILS QUIETLY
sections.note: If a step breaks, you hear about it the same day with the failing node named. A silent scorecard is worse than no scorecard.

nodes.label: 1 - GHL Event: New Lead, Appointment, Call, Contract, Payment
nodes.notes: One webhook url. Each GHL workflow posts to it with an event_type.

nodes.label: 2 - Normalize the Event: Type, Contact, Rep, Amount, Time
nodes.notes: Same field names whatever the source, so nothing downstream has to special case.

nodes.label: 4b - GHL: Read the Appointment's Assigned User From the Calendar
nodes.notes: The rep who took the call is the calendar event's assigned user, not the contact owner.

nodes.label: 5b - Unassigned Queue for a Human to Fix
nodes.notes: Never guess a rep. Park it, fix it, the nightly rollup picks it up.

nodes.label: 9 - Per Rep: Leads, Booked, Held, Contracts, Revenue
10 - Ratios: Booked per Lead, Held per Booked, Cash per Lead
11 - Update the Scorecard Tab, One Row per Rep per Day

output_sample.why: Appointment credited to the calendar event's assigned user Priya, not the contact owner Jordan
output_sample.slack_leaderboard: Scorecard for Sun Sep 21. 1. Priya 14 leads, 9 booked, 7 held, 78 percent held, 4 contracts, $9,600 booked, $686 cash per lead. 2. Jordan 16 leads, 8 booked, 5 held, 63 percent held, 3 contracts, $6,200 booked, $388 cash per lead.
output_sample.if_it_had_failed: Error trigger fires, Slack alert names the failing node and links the run, no row is silently skipped
